\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of NSPACE under constant rescaling]
\lean{Complexity.NSPACE.mono_const}
\label{Complexity.NSPACE.mono_const}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NSPACE}
\difficulty{3}
Let $s_1,s_2:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and let $a\in\mathbb{N}$. If $s_1(n)\le a s_2(n)$
for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, then $\mathrm{NSPACE}(s_1)\subseteq\mathrm{NSPACE}(s_2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Transfer from nondeterministic to banked preconditions]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.npre_of_npreS}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.npre_of_npreS}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.NARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.NPre, Complexity.LogProg.NPreS, Complexity.LogProg.Pre, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.bankStart, Complexity.LogProg.bankTM, Complexity.LogProg.bank_cleanRun, Complexity.LogProg.cleanRun_mono, Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_mono, Complexity.LogProg.length_callSegs_le, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle
deciders, let $M_j$ decide a language $L_j$ in space $s_j$ for each $j$, and fix an
input bit string $x$. Suppose $B,W_d\in\mathbb N$, $1\le B$, and for every $j,n$ with
$n\le 2|x|+2+m(2W_d+2)$ we have $s_j(n)\le B$. If a configuration $a$ satisfies the
nondeterministic precondition for $A$ on $x$, and every register value $v(r)$ in $a$ has
binary representation of length at most $W_d$ after adding $1$, then $a$ satisfies the
corresponding precondition for the banked machine that simulates all the deciders, using
the language indicators as its oracles and space bound $B$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Space Bound for Oracle Register Programs]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides_space}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides_space}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.NAns, Complexity.LogProg.NGuard, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts.mono, Complexity.LogProg.NPreS, Complexity.LogProg.bankK, Complexity.LogProg.bankStart, Complexity.LogProg.bankTM, Complexity.LogProg.narm_space, Complexity.LogProg.ncompileFinNDTM, Complexity.LogProg.npre_of_npreS, Complexity.NSPACE, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{5}
Let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let a nondeterministic register program
with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle languages have a finite control-state set with
decidable equality. Let $S,W:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and $C$ be a natural number, with
$1\le S(n)$ and $W(n)\le C S(n)$ for every $n$. Suppose each oracle language $A_j$ is
decided by a deterministic machine using at most $s_j(n)$ space on inputs of length $n$.
Assume that whenever $v\le 2n+2+m(2W(n)+2)$, one has $s_j(v)\le C S(n)$ for every $j,n$.
For some input-independent natural bound $N$ (which may depend on the input), suppose
that on each input $x$ every choice string of length $N$ makes the program halt, and
every configuration before step $N$ satisfies the program's validity conditions and has
each register's binary representation of its value plus one of length at most $W(|x|)$.
If $x\in L$ exactly when some length-$N$ choice string makes the program answer yes,
then $L$ belongs to $\text{NSPACE}(S)$: it is decidable in nondeterministic space bounded
by a constant multiple of $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nondeterministic logarithmic-space decision]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE, Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.NAns, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts, Complexity.LogProg.NPreS, Complexity.LogProg.log_poly_bound, Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides_space, Complexity.NL, Complexity.logSpace, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{5}
Let $L$ be a language of binary strings, let $\Lambda$ be a finite set of machine
states with decidable equality, and let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine with
$m$ registers, $d$ oracle languages $(A_j)_{j<d}$, and initial state $l_0$. Suppose
every oracle language belongs to logarithmic space, and fix $K\in\mathbb{N}$. Assume
that for every input $x$ there is a natural number $N$ such that every sequence of $N$
nondeterministic choices from the initial configuration (state $l_0$, all registers
zero, and no answer recorded) halts; moreover, at every earlier prefix where the
computation has not halted, its configuration satisfies the machine's precondition and,
for every register $r$, the bit length of $r+1$ is at most $K(\lfloor\log_2
|x|\rfloor+1)$. Assume also that $x\in L$ if and only if some such sequence of $N$
choices leaves the answer true. Then $L$ belongs to nondeterministic logarithmic space.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomially Bounded Registers Yield Nondeterministic Logspace]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides_poly}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides_poly}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE, Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.NAns, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts.mono, Complexity.LogProg.NPreS, Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_le_log, Complexity.LogProg.log_poly_bound, Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides, Complexity.NL, Complexity.logSpace, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{4}
Let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let a nondeterministic register program
with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle languages have a finite control-state set with
decidable equality. Suppose every oracle language belongs to $\text{LOGSPACE}$. For some
natural numbers $C_0,c_0$, assume that for every input $x$ there is a length $N$ such
that every choice string of length $N$ makes the program halt, and each configuration
before step $N$ along such a run satisfies the program's validity conditions and has
every register value at most $C_0(|x|+1)^{c_0}$. Assume further that $x\in L$ exactly
when some length-$N$ choice string makes the program answer yes. Then $L$ belongs to
$\text{NL}$, the class of languages decidable in nondeterministic logarithmic space.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial Space from Register Computations]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides_npspace}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides_npspace}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.NAns, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts, Complexity.LogProg.NPreS, Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides_space, Complexity.NPSPACE, Complexity.NSPACE, Complexity.NSPACE.mono_const, Complexity.PSPACE, Complexity.succ_pow_le, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{6}
Let $L$ be a language of binary strings, let $\Lambda$ be a finite state set with
decidable equality, let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine with start state
$l_0$, and let $(A_j)_{j<d}$ be oracle languages, each decidable in polynomial space.
Suppose there are natural numbers $C_0,c_0$ such that for every input $x$ there is a
natural number $N$ for which every choice sequence of length $N$ from the initial
configuration (state $l_0$, all registers zero, and no answer recorded) halts, and every
active configuration at each earlier prefix satisfies both the machine's required
precondition and the bound $|\mathrm{bits}(r+1)|\le C_0(|x|+1)^{c_0}$ for every register
$r$. Suppose also that $x\in L$ exactly when some such length-$N$ choice sequence leaves
answer true. Then $L$ belongs to nondeterministic polynomial space.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Logspace Oracles Yield Polynomial Space]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides_npspace_of_logspace}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides_npspace_of_logspace}

with $m$ registers, $d$ oracle languages $A_j$, and a finite control-state type $\Lambda$
with decidable equality. Assume every $A_j$ belongs to $\mathrm{LOGSPACE}$. For natural
numbers $C_0,c_0$, suppose that for every input $x$ there is a length $N$
such that every choice string of length $N$ makes the program halt, and every

conditions and has each register's binary representation (of the register value plus

choice string of length $N$ makes the program answer yes. Then $L$ belongs to
